Earth hangs at the far end of a long chain of worlds: a ray of creation, reaching down from the Absolute.
Seven worlds, each inside the next. The Absolute. All worlds. All suns. Our sun. The planets. The earth. And the moon.
Nothing happens by one force alone. Every event needs three: one that acts, one that resists, and a third that reconciles them. Where the three meet, something new is born.
The Absolute is bound by a single law. The next world by three, then six, then twelve, then twenty-four. The earth by forty-eight. The moon by ninety-six.
With each step down, the laws multiply, and life grows heavier, more mechanical, less free. We live near the bottom of the ray.
From all the suns to our sun, from our sun to the planets, the force flows downward, world into world, the way a note descends a scale.
But every scale has a gap. Between the planets and the earth, the descending note stalls. The force cannot cross on its own.
So something was made to bridge it. A thin film of organic life was stretched across the earth, to catch what the planets send and carry it on.
Plants, animals, people: together they are the earth's sensitive organ, a living membrane that feels the heavens on the earth's behalf.
And each part of the film hears something different. A field of grass takes in one kind of influence. Fill the same field with people, and it takes in another.
The influence falls on living things, and they pass it on, changed, down into the body of the earth.
What travels down is planetary influence: the quiet pressure of the worlds above, on every living thing below.
And the film gives back. It sends out radiations of its own: one kind rising to the sun, another to the planets, another falling to the moon.
Worlds, gap and living film: one design.
